source.author: Rebecca Sload
source.title: The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan: Narrative of a Reverentially Terminated Mountain-Cave

findings.subject: Later-phase cave ceramics near the entrance
findings.assertion: Among 18 ceramic pieces considered for later Teotihuacan activity, 17 were nonphaseable and one was assigned to Xolalpan; none was assigned to Metepec. Four 1977 surface finds from entrance Tracts 10 and 11 consist of one Xolalpan olla, one Regular Thin Orange, one Coarse Thin Orange and one San Martín Orange sherd.
findings.source_locator: Sload 2020, printed pp.147-149, Table 5.4 and Figure 5.6 cited in text; collection Tracts 10/11
findings.evidence_type: published archaeological description; original monograph chapter text examined
findings.observed_vs_interpreted: Specific objects, contexts and masonry relationships reported by author; interpretative dating and ritual significance are not independently established
findings.limitations: Entrance surface collection is disturbed; Sload proposes fall-in or entrance backfill, not secure later cave reuse.
findings.place: Cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.educational_use: Detailed cave architecture and later-use investigation

findings.subject: Tentative Aztec black-on-red pottery in rodent burrow
findings.assertion: A 0.6 g rim sherd from TE28 Area C:West Layer 5f rodent burrow has a black rim, polished red exterior and dark-cored fine paste, described as resembling an Aztec black-on-red bowl.
findings.source_locator: Sload 2020, printed pp.147-149, TE28 C:West Layer 5f
findings.evidence_type: published archaeological description; original monograph chapter text examined
findings.observed_vs_interpreted: Specific objects, contexts and masonry relationships reported by author; interpretative dating and ritual significance are not independently established
findings.limitations: Identification is tentative; transport by animal, probe-hole intrusion or later disturbance precludes identifying an Aztec human visit.
findings.place: Cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.educational_use: Detailed cave architecture and later-use investigation

findings.subject: Second Narrowing has concrete-faced core and uncoated extensions
findings.assertion: The Second Narrowing has a concrete-coated middle section with two non-concrete-faced extensions. At its west end, a concrete floor continues beneath the masonry extension and concrete on the cave wall extends behind it, documenting an architectural sequence.
findings.source_locator: Sload 2020, printed pp.151-154, Figures 9.3-9.5 cited in text; Sload 1978a:55-58 referenced
findings.evidence_type: published archaeological description; original monograph chapter text examined
findings.observed_vs_interpreted: Specific objects, contexts and masonry relationships reported by author; interpretative dating and ritual significance are not independently established
findings.limitations: Later than concrete is a relative stratigraphic inference; assigning the extensions after ceremonial termination is author hypothesis.
findings.place: Cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.educational_use: Detailed cave architecture and later-use investigation

findings.subject: Laja Passage two-phase construction and 15 cm floor remnant
findings.assertion: Laja Passage has an eastern concrete-faced section and western mud-mortared stone section. The publication reports Drewitt's excavation of an intact 15 cm wide concrete floor strip at its east end, and three finger impressions in mud mortar above the western entrance.
findings.source_locator: Sload 2020, printed pp.153-155, Figure 9.6 cited; Drewitt 1978:3 and Millon drawing cited but not consulted
findings.evidence_type: published archaeological description; original monograph chapter text examined
findings.observed_vs_interpreted: Specific objects, contexts and masonry relationships reported by author; interpretative dating and ritual significance are not independently established
findings.limitations: Underlying 1978 field records and figures were not independently inspected; dates and ritual function remain unresolved.
findings.place: Cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.educational_use: Detailed cave architecture and later-use investigation

findings.subject: Fourth Narrowing overlies concrete at South Transverse Chamber
findings.assertion: The single-section Fourth Narrowing lacks concrete facing but its masonry covers concrete at the entrance of the South Transverse Chamber; a laja roof is reported. This shows masonry superposition consistent with later modification of the passage.
findings.source_locator: Sload 2020, printed pp.153-155, Figure 9.7 cited in text
findings.evidence_type: published archaeological description; original monograph chapter text examined
findings.observed_vs_interpreted: Specific objects, contexts and masonry relationships reported by author; interpretative dating and ritual significance are not independently established
findings.limitations: Post-termination attribution depends on interpreting the earlier concrete phase as cave termination; not independently dated.
findings.place: Cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.educational_use: Detailed cave architecture and later-use investigation
